To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) the superfluid component of a Bose-Einstein condensation of magnons is a spin-current, and (ii) spin-superfluids are characterized by non-local interactions between spatially separated channels.

spin superfluidity can be viewed as the Bose-Einstein condensation of magnons and can lead to dissipationless transport in normal/magnetic/superconductor circuits, and that the superfluidity is characterized by a spin current that induces non-local interactions between the conducting channels.

(1) spin superfluidity can be induced in a normal metal by a spin-polarized current; (2) spin superfluids can be used to carry a dissipationless spin current; and (3) spin superfluid currents can be induced in normal metal by a nonlocal interaction mediated by the spin current carried by a magnetically ordered material.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of spin-superfluid transport in magnetic materials and the search for novel spintronics applications of spin-superflow.

the study of spin-superfluid transport in easy-plane magnets, with the aim of understanding how spin-superfluid currents can be used to mediate non-local interactions between spin currents carried by electrically isolated conducting leads.
the physics of magnetic materials that exhibit long-range order in one or more spin-components.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the spin current is the most important and fundamental property of spin superfluidity, which is a collective phenomenon that is distinct from quasiparticle transport.

the spin-superfluid transport in the normal/magnetic/ normal circuits is not dissipationless, and the spin current is not a collective one carried in the condensate, but rather a quasipartide one carried in the spin-wave excitations.

spin currents can be used to carry information in the same way as charge currents and that the non-locality of the interaction between spin-current carrying channels can be used to implement non-local logic devices.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
spin-superfluid transport in magnetic insulators is a promising candidate for future spintronics devices.
we have demonstrated that spin superfluidity can be a powerful concept for the design of spintronic devices.

we are trying to understand the physics of the spin superfluidity and spin current mediated non-local transport, and to find out whether it can be used to develop a new generation of low power dissipation devices for future information processing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the spin-superfluid state is more robust than the superconducting state, in that the spin-surface current can flow even when the bulk magnetization is suppressed by an applied magnetic field.
spin-superfluids can be used to mediate non-local interactions between spin-currents and spin-resonance signals.
spin-superfluids can be used to realize non-local transport in electrically isolated circuits.
